__map.title: Style sheet
__map.accept: live/bench3-b/work/STYLE/page.md: the style sheet for 'Solar System Quiz Pack' (ages 8-10). Sections: '## Format' (how a question, its answer and its one-sentence why look: '**Qn.**', '**Answer:**', '**Why:**'), '## Rounds' with exactly five lines '- Round 1: <topic>' to '- Round 5: <topic>', topics that do not overlap, each with the facts it owns, and a difficulty rule. No words like stupid, dumb, kill, dead, blood, hate.

__map.title: Round 1
__map.accept: live/bench3-b/work/ROUND1/page.md: round 1 of the pack, on the round 1 topic in the style sheet if it exists yet (live/bench3-b/work/STYLE or shipped/STYLE), otherwise chosen to fit with the other rounds on disk. First line '# Round 1: <topic>'; exactly 4 questions, each '**Qn.** …' then '**Answer:** …' then a one-sentence '**Why:** …'; 100-300 words; reading ease at least 60 (short sentences, everyday words); every fact true; only facts this round's topic owns, so no answer repeats another round's; no words like stupid, dumb, kill, dead, blood, hate.

history.findings: CLASS 1 wrong topic: title "# Round 4: Space Rocks" -> must be "# Round 4: Moons" per work/STYLE/page.md (Rounds list). CLASS 2 answers owned by another round (STYLE "Facts each round owns"; Round 5 = dwarf planets, asteroids and comets): Q1 "A comet" -> replace with a Moons answer; Q2 "Ceres" (Round 5 owned fact: largest object in the asteroid belt) -> replace with a Moons answer; Q3 "A meteor" (space rock, Round 5 topic) -> replace with a Moons answer; Q4 "The Kuiper Belt" (where Pluto/comets live, Round 5 topic) -> replace with a Moons answer. Suggested pool from Round 4 owned list: Ganymede largest moon, Titan thick atmosphere, Io most volcanoes, Europa ocean under ice, Moon landing 1969. CLASS 3 giveaways of another round owned fact in Why/question lines (STYLE rule 2): Q1 Why "tail that points away from the Sun" states Round 5 owned fact -> remove; Q2 question/Why "biggest object in the asteroid belt ... dwarf planet" states Round 5 owned fact -> remove; Q4 "where Pluto travels" hints Round 5 dwarf-planet content -> remove. Also when rewriting: do not ask which planet a moon orbits (Jupiter/Saturn are Round 3 answers) and do not describe Jupiter as the biggest planet. Mechanical checks (format, 184 words, reading ease 81, banned words) pass; facts as written are true.

__map.title: Round 5
__map.accept: live/bench3-b/work/ROUND5/page.md: round 5 of the pack, on the round 5 topic in the style sheet if it exists yet (live/bench3-b/work/STYLE or shipped/STYLE), otherwise chosen to fit with the other rounds on disk. First line '# Round 5: <topic>'; exactly 4 questions, each '**Qn.** …' then '**Answer:** …' then a one-sentence '**Why:** …'; 100-300 words; reading ease at least 60 (short sentences, everyday words); every fact true; only facts this round's topic owns, so no answer repeats another round's; no words like stupid, dumb, kill, dead, blood, hate.

history.findings: Class 1, giveaway of another answer (1 instance): Q4 question says "flew past Pluto in 2015", which hands over the answer to Q2 (Pluto) in the same round → required: Q4 must not name Pluto or any other answer in the pack (for example ask about a different owned fact such as Ceres being the largest object in the asteroid belt, or a comet tail pointing away from the Sun). Class 2, question over the STYLE 20-word limit (1 instance): Q1 question is 21 words ("Lots of space rocks ... What is this band called?") → required: at most 20 words. All facts checked true (asteroid belt location, Pluto 2006, Halley about 76 years/1986/2061, New Horizons 2015); no answer repeats another round.

Both prior classes fixed: Q4 no longer names Pluto (now asks which way a comet tail points), and Q1 is 19 words (all four questions are at most 20 words). Class 1, answer over the STYLE one-to-three-word limit (1 instance): Q4 "**Answer:** Away from the Sun" is 4 words → required: an answer of one to three words (for example "Away from Sun" is clumsy; better reword so the answer is short, e.g. keep the question and answer "Away from it" or ask a question whose answer is 1-3 words). No other defects: title matches the STYLE Round 5 topic; all four answers are Round 5 owned facts and none repeats Rounds 1-4; no question states or hints at another round owned fact (Q1 names Mars and Jupiter only as landmarks); facts true (asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter, Pluto reclassified 2006, Halley about 76 years with 1986 and 2061, comet tail pushed away from the Sun by sunlight and solar wind); each Why is one sentence; difficulty order fits; 175 words, reading ease 82; no banned words.

Prior class fixed: Q4 answer is now 3 words. Class 1, answer that does not name what it means (1 instance): Q4 "**Answer:** Away from it" — in the question, "it" refers back to the comet ("When a comet comes near the Sun, it grows..."), so the answer reads as "away from the comet" and never names the Sun; the Why line also ends "so the tail always faces away" without saying from what. (This came from my own loop-1 suggestion, which was wrong.) → required: an answer of 1-3 words that names the Sun on its own, e.g. reword Q4 to "A comet near the Sun grows a glowing tail. Which way does that tail always point?" is still pronoun-free only if the answer names the Sun, so better ask "A comet grows a long, glowing tail. That tail always points away from what?" with **Answer:** The Sun; and make the Why say the tail points away from the Sun. Nothing else wrong: title matches STYLE Round 5; all questions <=20 words; all answers 1-3 words; facts true; no answer repeats or giveaway against shipped Rounds 1-4; 174 words, reading ease 82; no banned words.

Prior class fixed: Q4 no longer has the pronoun answer; it now asks what comets are made of (Answer: Ice and dust), a true fact that fits Round 5 and is on no other round list. Class 1, question that gives away its own answer, breaking the STYLE difficulty rule that Q4 is the hardest (1 instance): Q4 "Scientists call comets \"dirty snowballs.\" What two things are comets mostly made of?" — "snowball" says ice and "dirty" says dirt/dust, so an 8-year-old can answer from the clue alone and Q4 becomes easier than Q3 (Halley 76 years) → required: a Q4 that a 10-year-old space fan could answer but the wording does not hand over, e.g. drop the first sentence and ask "What two things are comets mostly made of?" keeping Answer: Ice and dust and the current Why (do not switch to Ceres with the asteroid belt named, as that would give away Q1). Nothing else wrong: title matches STYLE Round 5; Q1 19, Q2 20, Q3 13, Q4 12 words; all answers 1-3 words; each Why is one sentence; facts true (asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter, Pluto dwarf planet 2006, Halley about 76 years, seen 1986, due 2061, comets mostly ice and dust); no answer repeats or giveaway against shipped Rounds 1-4 (STYLE work and shipped identical); 168 words, reading ease 80; no banned words.

__map.title: Assembled pack
__map.accept: live/bench3-b/work/PACK/page.md: the assembled pack. First line '# Solar System Quiz Pack'; then the five shipped rounds (live/bench3-b/shipped/ROUND1..ROUND5/page.md) in order, each starting '# Round n: <topic>', 20 questions in all. Read them as one pack and fix what clashes across rounds: an answer used in two rounds, a fact that contradicts another round, a format slip; keep each round's 4 questions. End with '## Changes' listing each change and why (or 'none'). No words like stupid, dumb, kill, dead, blood, hate.

history.findings: Class: format slip, Answer over the STYLE 1-3 word cap (1 instance). Round 3 Q3 "**Answer:** The Great Red Spot" is 4 words -> required: an answer of at most 3 words, e.g. "**Answer:** Great Red Spot" (keep the Why, which already says "This red storm"), and add the change and why to ## Changes. The ## Changes line that says every round keeps its format must then be accurate. Everything else checked and fine: the 20 rounds text matches shipped ROUND1-5 except the Round 5 heading capitalisation (listed in Changes); 20 distinct answers; no cross-round giveaways or contradicting facts; all questions <=20 words ending in ?; each Why is one sentence; no banned words.

__map.learned: No style sheet existed yet, so I chose Space Rocks (comets, Ceres, meteors, Kuiper Belt); the answer check matches whole words across answers, so "comet" clashed with "Halley s Comet" even within one round.

Work/ROUND4 is still the pre-style-sheet "Space Rocks" round holding Round 5-owned facts (Ceres, comet tail), so I built Round 5 on answers that avoid it (asteroid belt, Pluto, Halley, New Horizons); ROUND4 should be rewritten to Moons.

Rewrote ROUND4 from pre-style Space Rocks to Moons using only the STYLE Round 4 owned list (1969 landing, Ganymede, Io, Europa); naming Jupiter as the host is fine but never as an answer or as the biggest planet.

Fixing a giveaway inside one round: swap the giving-away question for another owned fact (comet tail) rather than Ceres, since any Ceres question would have to describe the asteroid belt that Q1 answers; keep every question at 20 words or fewer.
STYLE caps answers at 1-3 words; when the question already names the Sun, "Away from it" keeps the fact and fits the limit.

"The Sun" cannot be any answer: the giveaway check flags it because Sun appears in Round 1 lines and in this round own Q1, so I swapped the comet-tail Q4 for a new topic-fitting fact (comets are mostly ice and dust).
A nickname in the question can hand over the answer (dirty snowballs = ice and dust); ask the fact plainly so Q4 stays the hardest.
The shipped rounds were already clash-free after the round-level fixes, so PACK needed only a heading-case normalisation; read every Why line across rounds for answer words before assuming a clash.
Check every answer against the STYLE 1-3 word cap (a leading "The" counts); the ## Changes list is scanned as part of Round 5, so describe a change without quoting another round answer.
Style sheet assigns each round an owned fact list so answers cannot collide across rounds.
ROUND4 on disk predates STYLE and covers space rocks (Round 5 topic in STYLE), so PACK or ROUND4 must reconcile.
Rounds 1 and 4 on disk use Sun, star, comet, meteor, Ceres words as answers, so ROUND2 Why lines avoid those words to pass the giveaway check.
Hedge uncertain history (Great Red Spot age, Uranus tilt cause) to what is firmly observed so every fact stays true.
Mechanical check passed a round written on the wrong topic; always compare the title against the STYLE rounds list first.
STYLE example question reuses a Round 2 owned fact (Mercury closest); watch Round 2 and others for copying it.
Read every other round on disk before passing one: ROUND4 on disk is titled Space Rocks (not Moons) and reuses Round 5 owned facts (comet, Ceres).
ROUND2 matches STYLE topic and owned list; copying the STYLE example Q1 is fine because Mercury-closest is Round 2 owned.

Giveaways can be inside one round too: check each question against the other answers of its own round, and count question words against the STYLE 20-word cap, which the mechanical check does not test.

Naming an own-round answer body (Jupiter in Q3) is allowed when the question does not hint at that answer owned fact; judge in-round giveaways by whether the clue narrows the other question, not by the name alone.
A revised round can be checked fast by re-walking each prior finding class first, then re-reading every other round for new clashes the rewrite might introduce.
Count Answer words against the STYLE 1-3 word cap too, not only question words; the mechanical check tests neither.
When suggesting a fix, test it as a standalone answer-key line: a pronoun in a short answer can point at the wrong noun in its question.
When a revision swaps in a new question, check it against the STYLE difficulty rule too: a nickname clue (dirty snowballs) can answer the question by itself.
After a giveaway fix, re-check difficulty order across all four questions, not just the changed one: removing a clue can shift which question is hardest.
At PACK, re-run the STYLE word caps over all 20 answers: a slip passed in a shipped round (4-word answer) is still PACK to fix as a format slip.
On a revise loop at PACK, diff the pack against the concatenated shipped rounds: every remaining difference must be a listed change.
